_comment: The dead god's unanswered correspondence. Four letters, one per god, each opening
that world's questline when it is delivered.
THREE OPEN WITH A NAME. THE FOURTH OPENS `To --`. That is locked in WORLD.md and
enforced in core/ by Post, because no single letter can be checked against it: an
unaddressed letter is legal (exactly one must be) and an addressed one is legal too.
The invariant only exists once you have all four.
The names -- Rill, Ballast, Ash -- appear NOWHERE else in the mod, and a check
enforces that. The payoff is that you spend a hundred hours calling it The Verdant,
open the mail you are carrying, and read 'Rill --'. If the name has leaked into a
villager's line or a Warden docket somewhere, the reveal is already spent.
VOICE. The dead god speaks in procedure, because that is where the Wardens got it:
every flat authorised line a unit has said all game is inherited. So these are not
laments. They are correspondence between colleagues who have stopped speaking, filed
by somebody who only has one register and is using it to say something else.
They may NOT explain the plot. A letter that told you what happened would make the
search retroactively pointless -- the same constraint the last letter is built on.
